regions.name: Middle East
overview: The Houthi campaign against Saudi Arabia continued at high intensity. On 24 October the Houthis announced seven operations against airports, Aramco sites and bases from Riyadh and Yanbu to Dammam, Najran and Khamis Mushait. The next day debris from intercepted missiles fell in the Mecca province (Jeddah, Taif, Rabigh) and injured two people in Khamis Mushait. On 26 October the coalition said it had destroyed missile tunnels, launchers and a depot in Yemen. The same day Egypt's parliament authorised Sisi to provide military support to defend Saudi territory, and the WHO and OCHA warned that Taiz's health system was close to collapse.

The Iran–US war is paused but unresolved. The IRGC claimed that seven tankers were hit in one night (22 October) and that a further tanker struck a mine east of Hormuz on 27 October; none of these claims was independently verified. Iran's chief of staff said US warships would be fired on if they approached, and Brent rose to about $117. Trump is openly weighing a second 'Epic Fury'. At the same time, Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish security chiefs met Iranian officials in Tehran on 26 October to try to prevent renewed war, and on 29 October Trump said he had approved Vance's outreach to Tehran.

Israel voted on 27 October without a decisive result. With about 90% of votes counted, Netanyahu's bloc had 53 seats, Eisenkot's bloc 48 and the Arab parties a record 19. Final results are expected on 4 November, and coalition talks could take weeks. Before the vote, a Palestinian attack near Hebron on 23 October killed two soldiers, and Israel answered by locking down Hebron and imposing a 'full lockdown' on the West Bank. Gaza deaths continued under the ceasefire, with 13 killed in 24 hours on 25–26 October according to civil defence. Israeli shelling and demolitions in south Lebanon also continued, and a raid in Daraa killed a disabled man.

A new flashpoint opened on the Jordan–Syria axis. Gunmen killed nine people at a church funeral in Karak on 23 October, the deadliest terrorist attack in Jordan in years. On 26 October Jordan struck what it called militant hideouts in southern Syria, and Damascus said 5–8 civilians were killed without any coordination with it; the Nassib crossing was closed for a day and has since reopened. Elsewhere, drones were shot down over Baghdad's Green Zone on 27 October, an oil spill linked to the Hormuz war closed beaches in three UAE emirates, and Iraq's prime minister visited Damascus on 28 October.

countries.name: Gaza
incidents: 26 Oct — Khan Younis (al-Mawasi) / Gaza City (Rimal): Israeli strikes killed five people, including a 7-year-old girl, in a displaced persons' camp, in a tent near Khan Younis and in Rimal; civil defence said 13 were killed and about 60 wounded across the Strip in 24 hours.
26 Oct — Eastern Deir al-Balah: According to a security source, Israeli tanks and military vehicles advanced into an area west of the 'Yellow Line'.
28 Oct — Gaza Strip: Displaced families prepared for a fourth winter in camps as the fuel and shelter shortages continued.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Deadly Israeli fire continues almost daily under the nominal ceasefire: 13 people were killed in a single 24-hour period on 25–26 October. Israeli forces are also pushing beyond the 'Yellow Line' in Deir al-Balah, a creeping expansion of the zone they hold, which already covers about 63% of the Strip. Phase two of the ceasefire remains frozen, and Israel's 27 October election produced no majority, so coalition talks will probably last into late November or beyond, leaving no government able to take decisions on Gaza. Over the next 90 days, expect continued drone strikes on camps and residential areas, more advances across the Yellow Line, and a severe winter humanitarian crisis, with fuel, medicine and shelter shortages. A renewed Israel–Iran or US–Iran war would further reduce aid access and international attention.

countries.name: Lebanon
incidents: 28 Oct — South Lebanon (Majdalzoun, al-Mansouri, Kounine, Baraashit, Zawtar al-Sharqiyeh): Israeli artillery shelled several villages after overnight detonations by Israeli forces in the border towns of Khiam, Tallousa and Bani Hayyan, according to Naharnet; no casualties were reported.
23 Oct — Nabatieh / Zawtar ash-Sharqiyah: Israeli air strikes hit the Nabatieh area and artillery fired near Zawtar ash-Sharqiyah, according to Al Jazeera.

27–28 Oct — South Lebanon / Beirut: Al Jazeera reported that farmers were harvesting olives under drones and warplanes; President Aoun said on 28 Oct that only diplomatic negotiations could bring lasting peace, amid Lebanese press reports that Hezbollah had given the state no guarantees it would stay out of a new Iran war.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Israel still occupies more than 600 km² of the south and carries out near-daily strikes, artillery fire and demolitions. No deaths were confirmed in the reporting found this week, but the occupation and the pattern of attacks are unchanged, so there is no basis for a downgrade. The main risk over the next 90 days is that Hezbollah is drawn into renewed US/Israel–Iran hostilities. Hezbollah has given no guarantees of neutrality, although its sources say Iran told it to stay out. That would almost certainly trigger an Israeli air campaign against the Dahiyeh and the Bekaa. Separately, expect continued strikes, demolitions and civilian deaths from fire and unexploded ordnance in the south; friction between the state and Hezbollah over seized weapons depots; and a growing security gap as UNIFIL's mandate ends on 31 December. The new Israeli coalition is unlikely to soften policy on Lebanon.

countries.name: Iran
incidents: 22–27 Oct — Strait of Hormuz / Gulf: The IRGC claimed seven tankers were attacked or hit mines overnight into 22 Oct and said two more supertankers struck mines on 23 Oct; on 27 Oct it said another tanker hit a naval mine and exploded east of the strait (none independently verified; the US disputes Iran's mine claims).

24 Oct — Tehran: Chief of General Staff Ali Abdollahi said Iranian forces were ready to fire on US warships if they approached Iranian waters, and the IRGC threatened seabed internet cables if Iranian civilian infrastructure was hit again; Trump said on 23 Oct the US 'may do another Epic Fury'.

26 Oct — Tehran: Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin held security talks with Iranian officials aimed at preventing renewed war, and agreed to continue consultations.
29 Oct — Washington: Trump said he had approved Vice President Vance's outreach to Iran over 'medical supplies'.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The war with the US is in a tense pause. Iran keeps up its mine and tanker campaign at Hormuz, which has cut transits to a handful a day, and openly threatens US warships. Washington is weighing a second large strike campaign while keeping up the blockade and reinforcing with a third carrier group. There are new diplomatic tracks: the four-way Tehran security talks with Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye, Qatari mediation, and Vance's outreach, the first sign of US flexibility in weeks. Over the next 90 days, the most likely course is continued attacks on shipping and coercion at Hormuz. The risk of renewed US and/or Israeli strikes remains high after the 3 November US midterms and while Israel's caretaker government stays in place. Any such strikes would very likely bring Iranian missile fire at Israel and at US bases in the Gulf and Jordan. Continued repression at home, including espionage arrests and executions, is also likely.

countries.name: Yemen
incidents: 24 Oct — Aden: About four Houthi ballistic missiles struck the city; one hit the Coast Guard headquarters in al-Tawahi and others landed near Aden International Airport and in Khormaksar. The Transport Ministry called it the fourth attack on the airport this month.

24 Oct — Hamdan (Sanaa province) / Mocha: Saudi-led air strikes hit Houthi-held areas, and Houthi-run al-Masirah TV said strikes on housing for cement-factory workers killed 8 people and wounded more than 10; the Houthis claimed about 100 strikes in 24 hours.

26 Oct — Houthi-held Yemen: The coalition said it destroyed five missile storage tunnels, four ballistic missile launchers and a depot; on 25 Oct the government claimed 736 strikes and 307 Houthis 'neutralised' in 24 hours (unverified).
23–24 Oct — Taiz: OCHA said the city had been cut off for 20 days and that 'the clock is running out'; the Republican Hospital suspended some departments and warned of complete collapse within days.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Full-scale war continues. The government's 'Dawn of Yemen' offensive and coalition air power, which claims hundreds of strikes a day, face a Houthi siege of Taiz and repeated ballistic missile fire on Aden. The humanitarian situation in Taiz is the most acute risk: hospitals are close to shutting down, and dialysis, intensive-care and neonatal patients are in danger. Over the next 90 days, expect grinding battles on the Taiz, Lahij, Marib and al-Jawf fronts with no decisive breakthrough, continued Houthi strikes on Aden and Mukalla, and intensified coalition strikes on missile infrastructure. Mass civilian deaths in Taiz are a real possibility unless a humanitarian corridor opens. Egyptian support to Saudi Arabia, now authorised by Cairo's parliament, and the Tehran talks could create some diplomatic room, but a ceasefire is unlikely in the near term.

countries.name: Israel
incidents: 23 Oct — Near Hebron (West Bank): Two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three at a junction near Hebron before being killed; Israel locked down Hebron, displaced about 1,500–2,200 residents and imposed a 'full lockdown' on the West Bank, with about 70 arrests in at least 15 areas.

27–28 Oct — Nationwide: Israel's election gave no majority. With about 90% counted, Netanyahu's bloc had 53 seats, Eisenkot's bloc 48 and Arab parties a record 19; about 430,000–480,000 'double envelope' ballots were still to be counted, and final results are due on 4 November. Opposition candidates reported harassment on election day.
28–29 Oct — West Bank: Israeli raids continued as the Hebron lockdown entered its sixth day; on 29 Oct activists accused settlers of new assaults.
27 Oct — Egyptian border: The IDF detained an Egyptian national who had crossed the border into Israel.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No missile or drone attacks on Israeli territory were found this week. The deadly Hebron attack and the West Bank-wide lockdown that followed meet the definition of recurring deadly violence by armed groups, but not of hostilities on Israel's own territory. The risk of escalation is still elevated. A caretaker government led by Netanyahu will stay in office through what will probably be long coalition talks, while Washington weighs new strikes on Iran and Iran threatens to retaliate. Over the next 90 days, an Israeli or US strike on Iran would very likely bring Iranian missile fire at Israel, and possibly attacks by Hezbollah and the Houthis, which would move Israel to CRITICAL. Expect more Palestinian attacks and Israeli collective measures in Hebron and the northern West Bank, continued settler violence, and sharp political polarisation over the Arab parties' role in any government.

countries.name: Iraq
incidents: 27 Oct — Baghdad (Green Zone): Air defences at the US Embassy shot down two suspected reconnaissance drones, according to Iraqi security sources; the Security Media Cell reported one. Debris fell near al-Rasheed Street, the Shorja market and Kadhimiya, and no casualties were reported. It was the first such incident in many months.
21–23 Oct — Kirkuk province: Coalition air strikes killed 10 ISIS militants southwest of Kirkuk and six more in the west of the province, according to Iraqi security sources cited by Iraqi News.
28 Oct — Damascus: PM Ali al-Zaidi met Ahmed al-Sharaa on a historic visit; they discussed restarting the Baniyas oil pipeline and security cooperation.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. ISIS remains active in the Kirkuk belt, requiring repeated coalition air strikes. Armed factions, Kataib Hezbollah among them, still resist disarmament, which has been postponed to June 2027. The drone incident over the Green Zone, less than a month after the coalition withdrawal, shows that the capital can still be hit. There is no sustained armed conflict on Iraqi territory, so the country does not meet CRITICAL. Over the next 90 days, the main risks are attacks on US diplomatic facilities if the war with Iran resumes, Israeli or US strikes on PMF sites, militias joining the campaign against Saudi Arabia, and attacks on tankers near Basra that hit oil exports. Rapprochement with Damascus, including the Baniyas pipeline and border security, is a modest stabilising factor.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
incidents: 24 Oct — Riyadh / Yanbu / Rabigh / Dammam / Najran / Khamis Mushait: The Houthis announced seven missile and drone operations against airports (King Khalid International in Riyadh, struck in two stages, and King Fahd International in Dammam), Aramco sites and a military base; the coalition intercepted missiles aimed at Riyadh, Taif and Yanbu and a drone over the Eastern Province.

25 Oct — Mecca province / Khamis Mushait / Ahad Rafidah: Debris from intercepted ballistic missiles fell in Jeddah, Taif, Rabigh and Wadi al-Mughammas (the Houthis denied targeting the holy cities); in Asir, debris injured 2 people and damaged three residential buildings and seven vehicles, and 10 ballistic missiles and a cruise missile aimed at the south were intercepted.
26 Oct — Cairo / Tehran: Egypt's parliament authorised military support to defend the kingdom, and Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman joined four-way security talks in Tehran.
27 Oct — Saudi airspace: The coalition said it again downed Houthi missiles and drones aimed at the kingdom; the Dakar Rally 2027 was moved out of Saudi Arabia because of the conflict.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Saudi Arabia is under daily Houthi missile and drone attack on its airports, energy infrastructure and southern cities. Debris now falls in the Mecca province, and civilian injuries and damage continue. Riyadh is answering with strikes on Houthi missile infrastructure and is building outside support: Egypt's parliament has authorised military support, and Riyadh has opened a parallel security channel with Iran through the Tehran talks. Over the next 90 days, expect continued salvos on Riyadh, the Eastern Province, Yanbu and Khamis Mushait, more casualties and damage from debris, recurring aviation disruption, departures of foreign workers and events, and possible deployment of Egyptian air-defence assets. The Tehran track could ease Iran's backing for the Houthis over time, but there is no sign of a ceasefire yet.

countries.name: Syria
incidents: 26 Oct — Southern Syria: Jordanian air strikes on what Amman called militant hideouts linked to the Karak church attack killed 5–8 people, according to Damascus, which said the dead were civilians, including women and children, and denied any coordination; Syria closed the Nassib crossing on 27 Oct and reopened it on 28 Oct.

22 Oct — Jamla (western Daraa): Israeli forces killed Mouaz Salama al-Ba'ir, a man with a disability, during an overnight raid and house searches; the IDF said troops fired on a suspect who approached them. Protests followed in several provinces on 23–24 Oct.
22 Oct — Damascus countryside: Two Syrian security officers were killed in a raid on an ISIS cell near Damascus.
26 Oct — Suwayda: The province remains outside government control, as the US signalled differences with Israel over its Syria policy.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. This week brought deaths from three different sources: an Israeli raid in Daraa, Jordanian air strikes in the south and an ISIS cell near Damascus. Israel continues to hold and expand its southern security zone, and Suwayda remains outside state control. Jordan's unilateral strikes create a new cross-border pressure on Damascus. Over the next 90 days, expect continued Israeli incursions and possibly further killings in Quneitra and Daraa, and more Jordanian strikes if Amman links further attacks to groups in southern Syria. Expect continued ISIS cell activity, flare-ups in Suwayda, and use of Syrian territory as a corridor if the Iran war resumes. Ties with Baghdad, including the Baniyas pipeline, are growing, but a security deal with Israel is unlikely before a new Israeli government forms.

countries.name: Egypt
incidents: 26 Oct — Cairo: Parliament authorised President Sisi, by a two-thirds majority, to provide military support in coordination with Riyadh to defend Saudi territory, sovereignty and holy sites; a regional official said this would not include ground troops, and the Social Democratic Party abstained.
27 Oct — Cairo: Authorities ordered the closure of the independent news site Mada Masr.
27 Oct — Sinai border: An Egyptian national was detained by the Israeli military after crossing the border.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No armed violence or terrorist attack on Egyptian territory was found. The parliamentary mandate turns the planned support for Saudi Arabia into a formal, though open-ended, military commitment. The closure of Mada Masr points to tighter domestic control as the mission begins. Over the next 90 days, the key indicators are the type and location of the assets deployed (most likely air defence and naval), any Houthi threats or attacks against Egyptian forces or Suez-bound shipping, and Iran's reaction. HIGH would apply if Egyptian forces come under direct attack, if the Houthis target Red Sea and Suez traffic, or if there is a significant terrorist incident in Sinai.

countries.name: Jordan
incidents: 23 Oct — Hammoud (Karak governorate): Masked gunmen opened fire on a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church, killing 9 people (the toll rose from 7) and wounding about 25–40; King Abdullah vowed 'the harshest penalties' and three days of national mourning were declared.

26 Oct — Karak: Security forces arrested three Jordanian suspects, all wounded, after a dawn shootout; the military linked them to 'terrorist groups' in southern Syria, but no group has claimed the attack.
26 Oct — Southern Syria: The Jordanian air force struck what it called militant hideouts; Damascus said 5–8 civilians were killed, and families of the dead denied any link to the church attack.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The Karak church massacre is the deadliest terrorist attack in Jordan in years, and Amman has answered with cross-border air strikes, which confirms HIGH: deadly violence by armed groups plus a credible risk of escalation. It is not CRITICAL because there is no sustained armed conflict on Jordanian territory, and no Iranian strikes have hit Jordan since 9 September. Over the next 90 days, expect a heavy security crackdown, possible further strikes in southern Syria, tension with Damascus over civilian deaths and border closures, and heightened protection for Christian sites. An Israeli or US strike on Iran would very likely bring renewed missile and drone fire on bases in Jordan and debris over its airspace, which would justify CRITICAL. Drug and weapons smuggling from Syria remains a constant threat.

countries.name: Libya
incidents: 20–22 Oct — Eastern Libya: The eastern-based parliament approved the 2019 maritime deal with Turkiye, drawing EU opposition; Al Jazeera described it on 29 Oct as a Turkish breakthrough in the east.

26–29 Oct — Benghazi / New York: Commentary highlighted Saddam Haftar's push to succeed his father; UNSMIL's mandate expires on 31 October, and no renewal vote was found by 29 October. No new armed clashes or attacks on energy infrastructure were found for 22–29 October.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No armed clashes or drone attacks were reported this week. The east's approval of the Turkiye maritime deal is a significant realignment, a sign of a Haftar–Ankara rapprochement, but it raises friction with Greece, Egypt and the EU rather than causing violence on Libyan soil. Over the next 90 days, watch the UNSMIL renewal (the mandate expires on 31 October), the Haftar succession, renewed fighting in Zawiya and Sorman, and drone attacks or blockades on oil and power infrastructure. Any of these on a sustained basis would justify HIGH.

countries.name: Tunisia
incidents: 22 Oct — Tunis (Ettadhamen) / Sfax governorate (Jebeniana, Agareb): Police fired tear gas at protesters who blocked roads, burned tyres and threw stones after the death of a man detained on suspicion of drug dealing; in Jebeniana a man died during a security chase, and students in Sfax protested a classmate's death. Reuters reported no casualties from the clashes.
24 Oct — Tunis: A further protest against President Saied followed the clashes, a week after thousands rallied on 17 Oct in the largest anti-Saied protest in years.
21 Oct — Tunis / Gabes: An opposition politician was jailed for four years over social media posts; the same day a Gabes court sentenced ten environmental activists over a 2020 protest.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained, at the upper end. Unrest is rising: the largest anti-Saied rally in years, rare clashes with police in Tunis and Sfax governorate after deaths linked to the security forces, and continued prison sentences for opposition figures and activists. However, there is no organised armed violence and no confirmed deaths from the clashes, so HIGH does not apply. Over the next 90 days, expect more protests driven by economic hardship and anger at the police, further prosecutions, and a risk of deadly escalation if security forces use more force. HIGH would apply if unrest becomes violent with deaths or spreads nationwide. There is also secondary risk from smuggling along the Libyan border.

regions.name: Ukraine/Russia
overview: The trilateral track is moving forward, but slowly and on Moscow's terms. The Kremlin said US-Russia-Ukraine talks will be held in Abu Dhabi after 4 November 'depending on battlefield conditions', and that Europeans were not invited. Zelensky said he expects a meeting by 10 November and is still waiting for Washington to set a date; Trump said a Putin-Zelensky meeting could come 'soon'. The US direction still favours Moscow: on 27 October the NYT reported that Washington is considering lifting sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund, the diesel deal continues, and Lavrov will attend the G20 ministerial in the US on 30–31 October despite being under US sanctions. The first concrete result was a US-mediated local ceasefire at Oleshky (Kherson) from 27 October to evacuate 1,700–2,000 civilians. As of 28 October no violations had been reported, and both sides agreed to at least monthly humanitarian deliveries.

The talks have not slowed the strikes. Overnight into 27 October, Russia hit Kyiv with S-400/Iskander ballistic missiles and 280 drones, hitting the Southern Bridge, a university campus and medical centres. Zelensky said Russia fired more than 100 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast in two weeks and called anti-ballistic interceptors Ukraine's most critical shortage. Ukraine kept up deep strikes: on 28 October drones reportedly hit the Azot chemical plant in Novomoskovsk and a steelworks in Lipetsk. Overnight into 29 October, a mass raid on the Moscow region (Ukrainian outlets cite 613 drones) led to restrictions at Vnukovo, Domodedovo and Zhukovsky. The ground war continues at high intensity: about 180–190 combat engagements a day, with the Pokrovsk axis the hottest and Russian gains in Zaporizhzhia Oblast.

The Black Sea campaign against shipping killed again. On 23 October a drone sank the Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv about 13 nm east of Constanța, leaving 1 dead and 3 missing. AP reporting counted at least seven other cargo ships attacked off Romania and Bulgaria this month. Romania's President Dan blamed Russia directly, and Romanian air-policing jets shot down two drones in Romanian territorial waters the next day. NATO is deploying extra aircraft, drones and radars, but whether Article 5 applies is unclear because most strikes happen in international waters. Türkiye said it will keep the Straits closed to warships while the war continues, and Erdoğan offered Trump help in reviving diplomacy.

On the periphery pressure is rising, but there are still no hostilities. In Moldova, a Russian Geran drone came down about 100 m from homes and near an energy facility at Kistelnița (Telenești) on 23 October; Chișinău expelled a Russian embassy staff member. Ukraine's border guards say Belarus still allows Russian drones to use signal relays on its territory but see no troop build-up, while Minsk's prisoner-for-sanctions talks with Washington continue. In Georgia, the Constitutional Court's party-ban hearings ran a sixth day (28 Oct) and were extended to 30 October, and thousands joined the 25 October 'Georgia without Ivanishvili' rally, which passed peacefully. Armenia's ruling party won the 25 October local elections after arrests of opposition candidates, and parliament ratified the TRIPP framework with the US (28 Oct). In Azerbaijan, former powerbroker Ramiz Mehdiyev received a 14-year suspended sentence for treason, and Putin called Baku a 'good partner'.

countries.name: Ukraine
incidents: 28 Oct — Kharkiv/Rivne/Sumy oblasts: Russia attacked overnight with an Iskander-M/S-400 missile and 88 drones. A drone strike on Kharkiv killed 1 and injured 4, a separate attack on residential buildings injured 5 including a child, and Kharkiv brought in emergency power cuts. One person was killed in an attack on a civilian site in Rivne Oblast. Two State Emergency Service deminers were killed in Sumy Oblast, and Konotop had been without power for five days after a strike on energy infrastructure (Ukrainska Pravda, Ukrinform).

27 Oct — Kyiv: An overnight attack with S-400/Iskander ballistic missiles launched from Bryansk Oblast and 280 drones killed at least 1 and injured 14–15. It hit the Southern Bridge, a university campus, an administrative building and medical centres, and disrupted metro service on the left bank. Zelensky said Russia had fired more than 100 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast in two weeks (DSNS, Kyiv Post).

27–28 Oct — Oleshky (Kherson Oblast): A local ceasefire mediated by the US (through Melania Trump) took effect on 27 October to allow evacuation and aid for the 1,700–2,000 civilians remaining in occupied Oleshky. Ombudsman Lubinets reported no violations for 30 hours, and the two sides agreed to humanitarian deliveries at least monthly (White House, Ukrainska Pravda, Meduza).

28 Oct — Front line: The General Staff reported 181 combat engagements and 188 guided bombs in one day, with the Pokrovsk axis the most intense (38 engagements). DeepState reported Russian advances near two villages in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, where 846 Russian attacks on 41 settlements were recorded on 27 October.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Ukraine remains under full-scale attack, with deadly strikes in several regions every day and an increasingly ballistic-heavy campaign against Kyiv. Over the next 90 days, expect Russia to concentrate Iskander/S-400 salvos on Kyiv's energy, bridges and transport ahead of winter, using up Ukraine's scarce anti-ballistic interceptors; the Dutch €500m air-defence package helps but does not close the gap. The Abu Dhabi trilateral, which Kyiv hopes to hold by 10 November and which Moscow makes conditional on 'battlefield conditions', is the main variable. The Oleshky truce shows that local humanitarian deals are possible, but a general or energy ceasefire is unlikely without major Ukrainian concessions. US signals (RDIF sanctions relief under consideration, the diesel deal, Europe excluded from the talks) increase pressure on Kyiv to accept a framework without full security guarantees. Expect Kyiv to keep its deep-strike campaign as leverage; domestic support is high, with 80% backing refinery strikes in polls. Expect pressure on Pokrovsk and Zaporizhzhia to continue, and Black Sea attacks on grain shipping to keep going. Watch whether the Oleshky model expands, the date of the Abu Dhabi talks, any Trump–Putin–Zelensky summit, and new Patriot/PAC-3 deliveries.

countries.name: Russia
incidents: 29 Oct — Moscow region: Ukraine launched a mass overnight drone raid on the capital region. Sobyanin reported at least 74 drones downed, later reports gave higher figures, and Ukrainian outlets cite 613 detected. Rosaviatsia restricted flights at Vnukovo, Domodedovo and Zhukovsky and turned back two flights from Türkiye. Residents reported explosions in Naro-Fominsk. No casualties were reported (Kyiv Post, Ukrinform, 112.ua).

28 Oct — Novomoskovsk (Tula Oblast)/Lipetsk: Drones reportedly hit the Azot chemical plant in Novomoskovsk, one of Russia's largest, and a fire broke out at a steelworks in Lipetsk after an attack. Ukrainian outlets cited photos and videos; official Russian damage assessments were not found. The same day, Ukrainian intelligence said Russia is building a launch site near Millerovo for up to 100 Geran drones a day (Ukrainska Pravda).

28 Oct — Moscow: The Kremlin said trilateral talks with the US and Ukraine will be held in Abu Dhabi after 4 November 'depending on battlefield conditions', and that Europeans were not invited. It confirmed that Lavrov will attend the G20 ministerial in the US on 30–31 October. On 27 October the NYT reported that the Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on the RDIF (Meduza, Ukrainska Pravda).

23 Oct — Black Sea (13 nm east of Constanța): A drone hit and sank the Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv, bound for Sulina, leaving 1 crew member dead and 3 missing. Romania's President Dan blamed Russia, and the next day Romanian air-policing jets shot down two drones in Romanian territorial waters. Moscow has not acknowledged involvement (AP).
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Russia is waging an active war, and its territory, from the Moscow region to Tula, Lipetsk and Tambov, is under mass drone attack almost every night, with repeated hits on chemical, metallurgical and energy sites. Over the next 90 days, expect the Kremlin to use the Abu Dhabi track to lock in US concessions (the sanctions hold, possible RDIF relief, the diesel deal, Lavrov's G20 attendance) while keeping talks conditional on battlefield conditions and Europe excluded. It is unlikely to concede on territory or agree to a full ceasefire. Small humanitarian deals such as Oleshky can be used to show goodwill. Expect a winter ballistic-missile campaign against Ukraine's grid, a larger Geran launch capacity (Millerovo), and continued deniable attacks on Black Sea shipping. Those attacks now involve direct Romanian accusations and NATO jets shooting down drones, which raises the risk of an incident with a NATO member. Expect Ukraine's deep strikes to keep disrupting Moscow airports, industry and fuel supply. Internal control is tightening, with proposals to limit foreign internet traffic and travel restrictions on draft-age men, and regime stability risk remains low.

countries.name: Belarus
incidents: 23 Oct — Ukraine–Belarus border: Ukraine's State Border Guard Service (spokesman Demchenko) said Belarus is still letting Russian Shahed/Gerbera drones use signal relays on its territory to route attacks toward western Ukraine. It reported no troop build-up and no signs of preparations for an attack from Belarus. The service repeated this assessment on 28 October (Kyiv Post, Ukrainska Pravda).

22 Oct — Minsk: Lukashenka convened senior officials to review progress in negotiations with the US. US envoy John Coale is reported to plan another visit to Minsk 'in about a month' to secure the release of hundreds more political prisoners (Charter'97).

16 Oct — Verkhnedvinsk district (Vitebsk region): Lukashenka ordered people's militia units in every village council, armed with assault rifles, grenades and machine guns, and announced a nationwide readiness inspection of the militia and territorial defence (UNITED24, TASS).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Re-tested against the definitions, Belarus has no hostilities on its own territory. Its profile remains military activity that creates tension: militarisation down to village level, readiness inspections, the Oreshnik deployment and indirect support for Russian strikes through drone relays, which Kyiv says is still active. Ukraine's border guards see no troop concentrations. Over the next 90 days, expect Minsk to keep trading prisoner releases with Washington for sanctions relief (a new Coale visit is expected around late November), while staying embedded in Russia's war effort through logistics, relays and airspace. Lithuania and Latvia face a winter balloon season and border friction, after a disputed Latvian border incident earlier this month. A rise to HIGH would require direct military coercion against NATO neighbours, a serious armed border incident, or Belarusian forces entering the war.

countries.name: Moldova
incidents: 23 Oct — Kistelnița (Telenești district): During a large Russian attack on Ukraine, a Russian Geran drone entered from Vinnytsia Oblast via the Transnistrian region (Camenca) and fell about 100 m from a residential building, near family homes and an energy facility. No casualties were reported. President Sandu called it Russia's 'latest dangerous act', and Moldova declared a member of the Russian embassy persona non grata (Kyiv Independent).

16 Oct — Dondușeni district (near Scăieni): A drone crashed and exploded in a field, with no casualties. This followed five drone airspace violations in under seven hours overnight on 15–16 October (Ukrainska Pravda, Eurointegration).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. This is the fourth drone to come down on Moldovan soil in under four weeks (Hîrbovăț 30 Sep, Geamăna 11 Oct, Dondușeni 16 Oct, Kistelnița 23 Oct), and the latest landed close to homes and an energy facility deep inside the country. Chișinău has escalated diplomatically by expelling a Russian diplomat. There are still no casualties and no deliberate attack on Moldova, so the HIGH threshold is not met. Over the next 90 days, expect more incursions and debris during every mass Russian attack on Vinnytsia and Odesa regions, more diplomatic steps against Moscow, faster EU-funded air surveillance and counter-drone purchases, and border-post shelters. Russian hybrid pressure (cyber, Gagauzia, a winter energy squeeze on Transnistria) will continue, and attacks on shipping off Romania threaten regional trade routes. A first drone fatality, damage to critical infrastructure, or a deliberate strike on Moldovan territory would warrant a review toward HIGH.

countries.name: Georgia
incidents: 28 Oct — Batumi: The Constitutional Court held a sixth day of hearings on Georgian Dream's lawsuit to ban five opposition forces. The court president dismissed as 'demagoguery' a Coalition for Change argument that the lawsuit echoes Russia's security doctrine, and every opposition motion so far has been rejected. Hearings were extended to 30 October, the Federalists are boycotting, and the legal deadline for a ruling is 24 June 2027 (JAMnews, Georgia Today).

25 Oct — Tbilisi: Thousands rallied outside Tbilisi State University under the slogan 'Georgia without Ivanishvili', launching a protest campaign by the nine-party Opposition Alliance that builds toward a major rally on 28 November. No violence or mass detentions were reported (JAMnews, SOVA).

21 Oct — Tbilisi: The government named First Deputy Foreign Minister Zurabashvili as the prime minister's special representative for relations with Russia, a post that had been vacant for almost a year.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There is no organised political violence: the 25 October rally drew thousands but passed peacefully, and repression still takes the form of administrative arrests and court cases. Over the next 90 days, expect the party-ban case to continue past 30 October in a court that has rejected every opposition motion. A ruling could come at any time before June 2027, and the government may time it around the protest cycle. Expect the Opposition Alliance's campaign to build toward 28 November, continued administrative detentions of journalists and activists, a deepening dispute with the EU and Council of Europe, and gradual normalisation with Moscow. A ban on the main opposition parties combined with large protests that are violently dispersed would justify a return to HIGH.

countries.name: Armenia
incidents: 25 Oct — 21 communities: Local elections were held, and the ruling Civil Contract and affiliated candidates won most communities. On 24 October, the day before the vote, Armenian media reported arrests of opposition candidates and supporters in three of the 21 communities. Afterwards, Pashinyan said 'foreign-controlled spy forces' had been 'eliminated' (JAMnews, Armenpress).

28 Oct — Yerevan: Parliament ratified the TRIPP (Trump Route) framework agreement with the US by 63 votes to 32, with only Civil Contract in favour. A TRIPP Development Company will be 74% US-owned and 26% Armenian-owned for an initial 49 years. The opposition argued the deal favours Azerbaijan; the charter and shareholder agreement are still to be negotiated (Armenpress).

21 Oct — Stepanavan (Lori): The Investigative Committee arrested 14 people, including Strong Armenia's candidate for community head, Arsen Gevorgyan, on electoral bribery charges ahead of the local vote (OC Media).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There are no hostilities and no fatal border incidents. Tensions this week were political: arrests of opposition figures around the local elections, and Pashinyan openly framing the opposition as a 'spy network', which deepens polarisation without significant violence so far. Over the next 90 days, expect TRIPP to move to presidential signature and charter talks, anchoring the US role in the Syunik corridor. That will irritate Moscow and Tehran. Expect Russia to keep increasing economic pressure through the EAEU suspension track (report due in December), trade restrictions and gas leverage, while Pashinyan avoids an open break. The peace track with Azerbaijan remains intact but long-term, and still blocked on Baku's demand to change the constitution. Repeated armed border incidents, a deliberate shooting, or violent unrest after arrests of opposition figures would warrant a review toward HIGH.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
incidents: 27 Oct — Baku: The verdict against former presidential chief of staff Ramiz Mehdiyev (88), delivered behind closed doors on 22 October, became public. He was sentenced to 14 years, suspended because of his age and health, for treason, attempting to seize power by force, money laundering and bribery. His assets will be confiscated (JAMnews, Trend, APA).

28 Oct — Moscow/Baku: Putin called Azerbaijan a 'good partner', pointing to growing energy cooperation. It is a notable thaw after the 2025 crisis in relations, and comes while Baku is in a public dispute with Türkiye over the school hijab rules (OC Media).

19 Oct — Baku: The Prosecutor General's Office put seven Türkiye-based commentators, presenters, a lawyer and social media figures on an international wanted list for calling for the violent seizure of power and inciting religious hatred in connection with the hijab protests (Armenpress).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There are no hostilities on Azerbaijani territory. The hijab protests have produced detentions (officially 37 in Baku; activists report more than 200), internet restrictions and prosecutions, not lethal violence, and no major new protest incident was found this week. Mehdiyev's suspended treason sentence closes the 'coup plot' case in a way that shows elite power has been consolidated around Aliyev, without making a martyr of him. Over the next 90 days, expect Baku to keep treating the hijab protests as foreign-driven extremism, with more in-absentia charges, entry bans and online restrictions. Expect it to balance a strained relationship with Ankara against a warming tone from Moscow and ties with Israel. The Armenia track is slow but stable, and TRIPP ratification in Yerevan fits Baku's corridor goals. Violent clashes during protests, or a pattern of armed incidents with Armenia or Iran, would warrant a review toward HIGH.

regions.name: Sahel
overview: Sudan's drone war against crowded civilian sites continued: on 26 October a drone strike on a night market in Nyala (South Darfur), blamed on the Sudanese army, killed between 21 (doctors) and 102 (Emergency Lawyers) people, and MSF said Nyala Teaching Hospital received 36 bodies and over 150 wounded. The UN human rights office counted at least 306 drone deaths in the first three weeks of October. On 22 October the army retook the Bukuri base in Blue Nile from the RSF–SPLM-N alliance, and on 28 October UN investigators said a steady flow of foreign arms and fighters is prolonging and spreading the war.

The Sudan war and gold disputes are spilling into Chad and Niger. A drone strike on Sudanese refugees at Bamina near Tiné (Chad) on 20 October killed four to five people, including two aid volunteers. In Tibesti, AFP reported on 28 October that at least 72 Chadian soldiers have been wounded in running battles with the Miski self-defence militia since 14 October. On 26 October Niger accused Chad and France of a 24 October drone strike at Emiloulou (Agadez) that killed two civilians; Chad denied it on 27 October and accused Niamey of harbouring Chadian rebels, opening a new bilateral crisis.

Algeria's parliament approved, and President Tebboune on 26 October ordered, a troop deployment to Madama in northern Niger to protect Algerian energy interests and the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline route: Algeria's first foreign deployment since 1973 and a sign of thaw with the AES. In Mali, FAMa air strikes hit suspected jihadist sites near Léré (Timbuktu) on 26 October and Diabaly (Ségou) on 27 October, while a second HRW report (22 October) documented a drone strike that killed eight civilians at Guélédié and torture of detainees at Sévaré. In Nigeria, bandits killed at least 62 people at Binnari in Taraba State on 23 October, and attacks continued in Plateau and Zamfara.

The reporting gap in the central Sahel persists: no independently verified attack in Niger's Tillabéri/Tahoua belt and none on state forces in Burkina Faso was found for 22–29 October, which reflects junta information blackouts rather than calm. All threat levels are unchanged: Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso, Sudan and Nigeria CRITICAL, Chad HIGH (with clear upward pressure from Tibesti and the Niger dispute), Mauritania MODERATE.

countries.name: Mali
incidents: 27 Oct — Near Diabaly, Ségou region: The army general staff said an Operation Dougoukoloko air strike about 24 km east of Diabaly destroyed a site holding several vehicles and motorbikes it described as important terrorist logistics; no casualty figure was given.

26 Oct — North-west of Léré, Timbuktu region: FAMa struck a gathering of about 15 suspected militants roughly 75 km north-west of Léré; the general staff reported no movement on the site afterwards but gave no toll.

22 Oct — Central Mali: In a second report in four days, Human Rights Watch said FAMa and the Africa Corps committed new abuses during renewed fighting, including a 16 Sep drone strike on Guélédié that killed eight civilians and the torture of detainees held in a metal container at the Sévaré base between May and August. Neither defence ministry responded.

18 Oct — Tagadayat, near Ménaka: Most recent major attack: IS Sahel gunmen killed about 48 mostly Tuareg (Idaksahak) civilians, apparently in retaliation for a pro-government strike on suspected informants.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: JNIM, the FLA and the Islamic State hold territory and carry out regular deadly attacks, and the army's continuing air campaign in Timbuktu and Ségou shows hostilities are ongoing even in a week without a reported mass-casualty attack. Over the next 90 days FAMa and the Africa Corps will likely consolidate around Kidal and push toward Aguelhok and Tessalit, while relying on drone and air strikes in the centre and west whose civilian toll, now documented in two HRW reports, will feed JNIM recruitment. JNIM remains the main threat to the state through garrison assaults, IEDs around Mopti/Sévaré and its fuel blockade on the Senegal and Sikasso corridors, with escorted tanker convoys a likely target as the dry season begins. IS Sahel reprisals against Tuareg and Daoussahak communities near Ménaka are likely to recur. Algeria's deployment to Niger and Bamako's presence at the Russia-Africa summit point to a widening set of partners, but no change in the junta's reliance on force.

countries.name: Niger
incidents: 26 Oct — Algiers/Madama: President Tebboune ordered the deployment of Algerian army units to Niger, after both chambers of parliament approved it on 25 Oct; the troops are to protect Algerian oil facilities and the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline route, reportedly at the former French base at Madama, but numbers and timing were not announced.

24 Oct — Emiloulou, Agadez region: A night drone strike killed two civilians and wounded several. On 26 Oct the government blamed Chad and France, called it military aggression, summoned Chad's ambassador and said it would refer the case to the UN Security Council and the AU; Chad denied involvement on 27 Oct.
22–29 Oct — Tillabéri/Tahoua: No independently verified attack on state forces was found; the junta's restrictions on reporting mean this is an information gap, not a lull.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: the threat has not decreased. ISSP mass-casualty attacks in late September, the August mutiny and the continuing army purge point to sustained insurgency and acute regime instability, and a further week without verified reporting does not indicate calm. Over the next 90 days ISSP ambushes on army and gendarmerie convoys in Tillabéri and attacks in the Tahoua–Dosso belt are likely to continue, with JNIM pressure in the south-west toward Benin and Boko Haram attacks around Diffa. The Emiloulou strike opens a new front of tension with Chad: Niamey is likely to use it to rally domestic support against alleged French interference, and N'Djamena's counter-accusation that Niger harbours Chadian rebels raises the risk of proxy activity in the north. An Algerian force at Madama would add a new foreign military actor in the north and may ease Niamey's isolation, but will not affect the insurgency in the south-west. The risk of another coup or mutiny remains realistic.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
incidents: 22–29 Oct — Nationwide: No independently verified attack on army or VDP positions was found, in line with the junta's continuing information blackout on jihadist attacks.

20–21 Oct — Ouagadougou: The transitional legislature unanimously adopted a revised criminal code that reinstates the death penalty for terrorism, treason and espionage; Traoré framed it as the end of "sentimentalism", and rights groups had warned against it.

16 Oct — Oudalan province: Most recent major reported fighting: IS Sahel claimed to have killed more than 400 JNIM fighters at Ganadaouri in clashes that began on 9 Oct; the figure remains unverified.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: two jihadist groups fight the state and each other across much of the country, and the absence of reported attacks reflects the blackout, not calm. Over the next 90 days the JNIM–IS Sahel contest for Oudalan and Liptako-Gourma will likely keep producing high-casualty clashes, while JNIM keeps overrunning army and VDP posts in the North, East and Boucle du Mouhoun and keeps up the sieges of Djibo, Sebba and Titao; large garrison assaults are likely as the dry season sets in. The death-penalty law points to tighter repression of dissent and suspected collaborators and could be used against officers accused of plotting. Analysts should rely on group claims, displacement data and cross-border reporting, and watch for instability inside the junta.

countries.name: Sudan
incidents: 27 Oct — El Leri area, South Kordofan: Drone strikes on three gold-mining sites killed at least five people and wounded several; no party claimed them, though mining authorities have previously blamed the RSF for attacks on mines in the state.

26 Oct — Nyala, South Darfur: A drone strike on a crowded night market killed between 21 (doctors) and 102 (Emergency Lawyers) people and wounded more than 100; MSF said Nyala Teaching Hospital received 36 bodies and over 150 wounded. Rights groups and the RSF-led Tasis government blamed the army, and an army-allied force said it hit an RSF camp.

22 Oct — Blue Nile: The army said it recaptured two areas, including the strategic Bukuri base, from the RSF–SPLM-N alliance after heavy clashes, following attacks it repelled at Al-Baraka (Kurmuk) on 19 Oct and in the east of the state on 20 Oct; the fighting has displaced about 27,400 families.

28 Oct — New York: The UN fact-finding mission said a steady flow of foreign weapons and fighters is prolonging the war and spreading it geographically; the UN rights office had counted at least 306 drone-strike deaths in the first three weeks of October.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: full-scale war continues on several fronts, with mass-casualty drone strikes by both sides on markets, mines and transport hubs. Over the next 90 days the army is likely to keep up near-daily air and drone strikes on RSF-held cities in Darfur and Kordofan, with further mass-casualty incidents like Nyala, al-Dabab and Abyei, while the RSF continues drone attacks on El Obeid and army-held cities and may still attempt a siege of El Obeid. Blue Nile has become an active front: the army's Bukuri gain is likely to be contested by the RSF–SPLM-N alliance near Kurmuk and Geissan, with Khartoum's accusation that Ethiopia hosts drones raising cross-border risk. Drone strikes on Chad's border zone and the Abyei strike show the war is spreading beyond Sudan. With foreign arms flows continuing and al-Burhan rejecting talks, a truce is unlikely; expect more displacement into Chad and South Sudan and deepening famine.

countries.name: Chad
incidents: 28 Oct — Tibesti: AFP reported that at least 72 soldiers have been wounded and evacuated to N'Djamena since running battles began with the Miski Self-Defence Committee on 14 Oct; the militia says Miski remains under its control and accuses the government of breaking the 2025 peace deal by imposing gold levies. The government has made no official statement.

27 Oct — N'Djamena: Government spokesman Gassim Chérif Mahamat rejected Niger's accusation that Chad carried out or supported the 24 Oct drone strike at Emiloulou (Agadez), demanded that Niamey publish its evidence, backed an international inquiry and accused Niger of harbouring Chadian rebel groups.

20 Oct — Bamina, near Tiné (Ouaddaï/Wadi Fira border): A drone strike on a gathering of Sudanese refugees killed four (Chadian government) to five people (Sudanese Emergency Rooms Council), including two aid volunteers, and wounded 14; Chad called the drone of unknown origin and opened an investigation, while local volunteers blamed the RSF.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained, with upward pressure: Chad now faces sustained clashes between the army and an armed militia that holds the town of Miski, a repeat cross-border drone strike from the Sudan war, Boko Haram around Lake Chad and deadly intercommunal violence in the south-east. It is not raised to CRITICAL because the Tibesti fighting is confined to one mining area, confirmed deaths since 14 Oct remain limited (two officers on the first day; no further official toll), and the state retains control of the wider territory. Over the next 90 days the army is likely to try to retake Miski by force, which could produce a confirmed high death toll and draw in Tibesti Toubou networks and Libyan-based rebels; that, sustained weekly deadly clashes, or a repeat of large cross-border strikes would justify CRITICAL. The dispute with Niger is likely to escalate rhetorically and could lead to mutual support for rebel groups along the shared northern border. Dry-season transhumance will likely bring more farmer–herder violence in Salamat and Ouaddaï, and refugee arrivals at Tiné and Adré will stay high.

countries.name: Mauritania
incidents: 28 Oct — Atlantic coast: The government said it rescued more than 200 migrants, including 28 minors, from a boat that had left Gambia, less than a week after another operation rescued more than 190.
27 Oct — Nouakchott: University students boycotted classes to protest an increase in subsidised transport fares from 5 to 30 ouguiyas; no violence was reported.

22–29 Oct — Hodh Chargui/Mali border: No new security incident on Mauritanian territory was found; a regional IOM-linked assessment published 22 Oct described the border zone as under growing pressure, hosting more than 300,000 Malian refugees.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained: Mauritania has no organised armed violence on its own territory; its risk comes from border friction with Mali, refugee pressure, migration and limited social unrest. Over the next 90 days FAMa and Africa Corps air strikes in Timbuktu and Ségou regions, close to the border, and JNIM activity in western Mali are likely to push more refugees into Hodh Chargui and raise the risk of drone or ground incidents involving Mauritanian herders, keeping relations with Bamako tense. Nouakchott will likely stick to containment through diplomatic protests and precautionary measures, while migrant interdictions on the Atlantic route continue. Cost-of-living protests such as the student boycott are a minor domestic risk. A JNIM attack inside Mauritania or an armed border clash would justify HIGH.

countries.name: Nigeria
incidents: 23 Oct — Binnari, Karim-Lamido LGA, Taraba: Gunmen described as bandits attacked the village on market day, killing at least 62 people and wounding 52 according to NEMA; 15 of 52 recovered bodies were pulled from the Benue River after residents fled into it, and police said the toll was not final.

27 Oct — Gero (Gyero), Jos South LGA, Plateau: Gunmen opened fire on residents before dawn, killing six according to police (seven per the community); the governor vowed to track down the attackers, after a further killing of an NSCDC officer in Mangu on 19 Oct.

25 Oct — Targejeri crossing, Kaga LGA, Borno: The army said troops of 29 Task Force Brigade ambushed ISWAP fighters and killed six; separately, on 23–24 Oct gunmen attacked Kaura Namoda, Zamfara, killing seven residents and abducting several.

17 Oct — Gamboru Ngala–Cameroon border road, Borno: Most recent major attack on the army: a landmine and ambush on a patrol killed about 10 soldiers and 5 CJTF members, according to soldiers who spoke to Reuters.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: three costly ISWAP or Boko Haram attacks on army positions in Borno in October, a mass-casualty bandit massacre in Taraba and continuing killings in Plateau and Zamfara confirm sustained insurgency and large-scale armed violence across several regions. Over the next 90 days ISWAP is likely to keep up night raids on isolated forward bases in Guzamala, Kukawa, Marte and Abadam as the dry season improves mobility, along with IED and ambush attacks on supply routes toward Cameroon, while the military relies on air and artillery strikes of uncertain effect. Bandit violence is spreading beyond the north-west into Taraba and the middle belt, and attacks on Plateau's Jos South, Bokkos and Mangu areas risk reprisals. These security failures will add to political pressure ahead of the election cycle.

regions.name: Asia-Pacific
overview: The Korean peninsula has moved from words to visible force on the border. On 25–26 October Yonhap and a Reuters witness saw three North Korean 122 mm self-propelled howitzers in open positions on the Kaepung coast, barrels pointed south toward Gimpo, while 20–30 soldiers built fences inside the DMZ. The same weekend Pyongyang told the UN Security Council that the September mine blast was a South Korean 'fabrication' and that it could invoke self-defence. On 29 October, the last day of Keen Sword, it fired an unidentified projectile into the East Sea, its fourth known launch event in October. Kim Yo Jong's end-of-October deadline for running loudspeakers along the whole border is about to expire.

Pakistan's two-front war widened this week. On 22 October the BLF launched 'Operation Almas' in Gwadar, with a vehicle-borne suicide attack on the Frontier Works Organisation camp and attacks on a police station and a convoy. The BLF claims more than 80 personnel killed; the military reports 10 militants and one civilian dead and no losses of its own. In KP, two soldiers died in a DI Khan operation on 24 October and four police in Karak on 22 October. On the Durand Line, Afghan Taliban mortar fire killed a civilian at Angoor Adda on 27 October, and Islamabad says it destroyed seven Taliban posts in response.

PLA pressure across the first island chain stayed constant but lower-key. The Liaoning carrier group sailed through the Basilan Strait and the Sulu and Celebes seas on 22–26 October, passing 15–50 nm off Mindanao without answering Philippine radio challenges. Chinese Y-9s and Russian Il-20s shadowed Keen Sword on 20–23 October. Around Taiwan, MND counts fell to single digits per day, but the PLA's first 'Taiwan Restoration Day' poster on 25 October and CCTV satellite imagery of Taiwanese cities kept up the political signalling. At sea, a Philippine fuel mission to Scarborough Shoal on 27 October passed without incident despite CCG and PLAN presence.

Myanmar's battle for Sittwe has become the region's most intense fight. A Y-12 bombing of downtown Sittwe on 23 October reportedly killed at least six people and wounded 37. The Arakan Army reportedly hit three junta warships at the Kaladan mouth on 26 October and sank two, and the regime's landing force on Nga Pyi Island is reportedly trapped. Junta air and gyrocopter strikes killed six women in Budalin and two people in Pauktaw on 22 October. Elsewhere violence was lethal but local: security forces shot dead two Papuan civilians in Nduga on 23 October, two men were beaten to death by a mob in Dhaka on 27 October, and Manipur stayed tense after the 19–20 October killings.

countries.name: North Korea
incidents: 29 Oct — Off the east coast: South Korea's military said North Korea fired an unidentified projectile toward the East Sea on the last day of Keen Sword, at least its fourth launch event in October after the 3 Oct hypersonic IRBM, the 11–12 Oct ballistic missiles and the 14 Oct submarine-launched cruise missiles. No further details had been released.

25–26 Oct — Kaepung county, west coast DMZ: Three 122 mm self-propelled howitzers were seen from the Aegibong Observatory (Gimpo) in exposed positions with barrels pointed south, one bearing anti-US slogans. A Reuters witness also saw 20–30 soldiers building fences inside the DMZ. The JCS said the North was 'deploying and exposing its older artillery pieces' (M-1981 type) along coastal areas.

25 Oct — New York (UNSC): In a letter to the Security Council, Pyongyang's UN envoy called the 21 Sep DMZ mine blast a South Korean 'fabrication' and a 'sinister obstructive move'. He defended the border fortification work as an exercise of sovereignty and warned that warning shots at its soldiers could trigger self-defence.

27 Oct — Pyongyang (via KCNA): Kim Jong Un told the 3rd Conference of KPA Company Commanders that units must maintain constant combat readiness through continuous, intensive training. Separately, CPPCC chairman Wang Huning met Kim in Dandong on 24 Oct for the Korean War anniversary.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Over the next 90 days, expect Pyongyang to make good on Kim Yo Jong's deadline by switching on loudspeakers along the border. It is also likely to keep exposed artillery and new 'tactical strike' assets forward and to continue fencing and road work that repeatedly crosses the MDL. Each crossing invites South Korean warning fire, which Pyongyang now explicitly frames as grounds for self-defence. This is the most likely route to a kinetic exchange. The 29 Oct launch shows testing continues alongside the border campaign, so expect further ballistic or cruise-missile launches around allied drills. The visible Chinese political embrace (Wang Huning visit) lowers the diplomatic cost of escalation for Pyongyang. A nuclear test remains a low-probability, high-impact wildcard.

countries.name: Myanmar
incidents: 26 Oct — Kaladan River mouth, Sittwe/Ponnagyun, Rakhine State: Citing military sources, DMG/BNI reported that the Arakan Army struck three junta warships, including a frigate, that were shelling Nga Pyi Island and nearby villages, and sank two of them. The junta answered with air raids and artillery on Nga Pyi, and fighting near Wahbo and Amyint Kyun continued on 28 Oct. The sinkings are not independently confirmed.

23 Oct — Sittwe, Rakhine State: A junta Y-12 aircraft reportedly bombed downtown Sittwe, killing at least six people and wounding 37 (BNI). Myanmar Now reported a blast in central Sittwe that killed at least two, with conflicting accounts of the cause. MSF called on all parties to protect civilians, and the remnants of a junta amphibious force were reported trapped on Nga Pyi Island.

22 Oct — Budalin Township, Sagaing / Pauktaw Township, Rakhine: A junta gyrocopter attack in Budalin killed six women, including a mother and her three daughters. A nighttime airstrike in Pauktaw killed two people and wounded six.

24–27 Oct — Southern Chin State / Indaw, Sagaing: Resistance forces said a roughly 500-strong junta column advancing on Kyindwe suffered nearly 200 casualties in ambushes, and Chin forces were still resisting the offensive on 27 Oct. Junta troops reportedly left more than 50 bodies behind after heavy losses in fighting around Indaw. These figures are resistance claims.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Over the next 90 days, the battle for Sittwe is the decisive front. The junta's amphibious attempt to break the AA siege via Nga Pyi Island is failing at a growing cost in vessels, and the AA has openly warned of retaliatory airstrikes on civilians. Expect intensified bombing of Sittwe, Pauktaw, Ponnagyun and Kyauktaw, possible mass-casualty strikes, and further AA attacks on naval units. A collapse of the naval defence of Sittwe would be a strategic turning point and would draw more Chinese involvement given nearby Kyaukphyu. Elsewhere, junta columns in southern Chin and Sagaing will keep taking heavy losses while the air campaign continues at roughly three civilian deaths a day. No negotiated de-escalation is in sight.

countries.name: Pakistan
incidents: 22–23 Oct — Gwadar, Balochistan: The BLF launched 'Operation Almas'. A vehicle-borne suicide bomb breached the Frontier Works Organisation camp at Zero Point, and fighters held positions there overnight while attacking Mazani police station and a convoy in Gabd. The BLF claims more than 80 military and intelligence personnel killed; Pakistan's military reported 10 militants and one civilian killed and no security losses. Neither account is verified.

27 Oct — Angoor Adda, South Waziristan, KP: Afghan Taliban mortar fire hit a house, killing one civilian and wounding five members of one family. The Information Ministry said Pakistan's response was 'immediate, effective and disproportionate' and destroyed seven Taliban posts, and on 28–29 Oct it rejected Kabul's account of the clash as fabricated.

24 Oct — Zarkani, Dera Ismail Khan, KP: The ISPR said six militants and two soldiers were killed in an intelligence-based operation. On 22 Oct, four police officers and two militants died in a raid on a militant commander's hideout near Latamber police station, Karak.

20–26 Oct — Balochistan (BLA claims): The BLA said it carried out 15 attacks that killed more than 27 personnel, including an ambush that killed four soldiers near the Gurgina grid station, Mastung, on 26 Oct and an IED that killed two in Kalat on 24 Oct. These claims are unverified.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Over the next 90 days, expect continued Pakistani–Afghan Taliban artillery and mortar duels along the Kurram–Paktia and South Waziristan sectors, with a real risk of renewed Pakistani air strikes in Afghanistan. Talks remain stalled. Baloch insurgents are escalating to complex, multi-day assaults on CPEC-linked infrastructure in Gwadar and say they will keep targeting CPEC, Reko Diq and Saindak. Expect further VBIED and ambush attacks, along with sharply diverging casualty claims. TTP and affiliate attacks on KP police and troops will continue at a high tempo. Governor's rule in KP and the PTI's demands for Imran Khan's release keep political unrest simmering. The PTI has avoided street protest for now after police fired on workers in Bara, but mass mobilisation remains possible.

countries.name: India
incidents: 20 Oct — Leimakhong / P. Molding, Kangpokpi, Manipur: A 44-year-old Kuki villager, Paolenmung Thangeo, was shot dead while collecting bamboo shoots. The Kuki Youth Organisation blamed NSCN-IM and ZUF cadres, which is unverified. The same day, a joint Manipur Police, CRPF and CoBRA team arrested three suspected Kuki militants over the 19 Oct killing of three Meitei villagers, and follow-up raids recovered 12 firearms, 1,099 rounds, grenades and an IED.

22–23 Oct — Imphal Valley / Sinai camp, Manipur: Protests and sit-ins spread across the Valley after a Joint Action Committee call, and security forces clashed with AISF members near Kangla Gate and detained several. On 23 Oct a security operation at Sinai camp found 18 people, verified one as a KNF cadre covered by earlier agreements and detained 17.

17 Oct — Jumgund, Keran sector, Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir: The most recent J&K incident found. Troops foiled an infiltration bid across the LoC, killing two infiltrators, and a search operation followed; no new J&K encounter was reported between 22 and 29 Oct.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Manipur shows recurring deadly violence on two axes, Kuki–Meitei in the Imphal valley foothills and Kuki–Naga in the hills, with more than 50 deaths in 2026. Suspension of Operations arrangements with Kuki groups have lapsed. Over the next 90 days, expect further tit-for-tat killings of villagers collecting firewood or forest produce, Valley protests and clashes with security forces, and arrests and raids on armed groups' camps. In Jammu and Kashmir, infiltration attempts in Kupwara, Poonch and Rajouri will continue until the snow closes the passes. India–Pakistan tension remains a background factor, but no direct military incident was reported.

countries.name: China
incidents: 22–26 Oct — Basilan Strait / Sulu and Celebes seas: The Liaoning, with destroyers Huainan, Wuxi and Anshan (ISW also reports Type 055 cruisers), passed off Zamboanga del Norte and Sarangani toward the Celebes Sea, coming 15–50 nm from Mindanao and ignoring Philippine radio challenges. Global Times called it routine Western Pacific training; ISW assesses it likely simulated a first-island-chain breakout.

25 Oct — Beijing / Eastern Theater Command: On the second 'Taiwan Restoration Day', the ETC issued its first poster urging Taiwan to 'come home', and a PLA expert said the PLA would 'deliver forceful blows' against separatism. TAO director Song Tao promoted a 10-point integration package, and CCTV released Jilin-1 high-resolution satellite imagery of Taiwan's cities and ports.

20–23 Oct — Ryukyu gaps: PLA Y-9 aircraft flew through the Okinawa–Miyako gap on 20 and 21 Oct to shadow Keen Sword, one reaching the waters off Amami Oshima, while Russian Il-20s flew toward Shimane on 22–23 Oct. Seven PLAN ships with replenishment support were assessed to be monitoring the exercise.
24 Oct — Dandong: CPPCC chairman Wang Huning met Kim Jong Un for the anniversary of China's Korean War entry, a high-profile show of political backing for Pyongyang amid the DMZ crisis.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. China's own territory faces no armed threat and internal security is stable. Over the next 90 days, expect Beijing to keep up its steady pressure in the grey zone and in the air. That includes carrier deployments that test the first island chain from the south (Philippines) as well as the north (Ryukyus), ISR shadowing of allied drills, and coast guard 'law enforcement' around Taiwan's outlying islands and the Philippines. The heavier political messaging on Taiwan, through the Restoration Day poster and satellite imagery, keeps a large named drill in the November–December window a meaningful possibility; none has been held in 2026. The main risk is a collision or confrontation involving Chinese forces at sea or in the air.

countries.name: Taiwan
incidents: 27–28 Oct — Around Taiwan: The MND tracked 6 PLA aircraft, 6 PLAN vessels and 1 official ship in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 28 Oct and deployed aircraft, ships and coastal missile systems. Its October totals so far reached 175 aircraft and 329 ship sightings.

25–26 Oct — Around Taiwan: The MND detected 3 PLA sorties (1 crossing the median line into the southwestern and eastern ADIZ), 6 PLAN vessels and 9 official ships. A day earlier, on 23 Oct, it reported no PLA aircraft at all, a sign of the low-tempo but persistent naval and coast guard presence.

25 Oct — Beijing / Taipei: China marked 'Taiwan Restoration Day' with an ETC poster in traditional characters urging Taiwan to 'come home', state-media satellite imagery of Taiwanese cities and ports, and a TAO integration package. Former KMT chair Hung Hsiu-chu attended the Beijing event and backed 'peaceful unification'.

16–21 Oct — Pratas (Dongsha): CCG ships repeatedly entered restricted waters around Pratas, one using 'dark ship' tactics with its AIS switched off. The CGA said it had carried out 15 expulsions on 12 occasions near Pratas in 2026, after driving away 16 Chinese ships around the main island and Pratas on 18 Oct.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Air activity eased this week, but the coercive structure is unchanged. Six to nine PLAN and official ships stay around the island every day, CCG incursions at Pratas and Kinmen continue, and Beijing has stepped up messaging on 'restoration' and unification. Over the next 90 days, the November–December peak training window is the most likely time for a named large-scale encirclement drill. A trigger could be a Washington decision on the frozen arms package or a step Beijing deems provocative. Expect continued grey-zone pressure on Pratas and Kinmen, cognitive and information operations, and further median-line crossings.

countries.name: Philippines
incidents: 27 Oct — Scarborough (Bajo de Masinloc) Shoal: BFAR vessel Mamalakaya, escorted by BRP Malapascua and a PCG aircraft, delivered fuel to 40–50 Filipino fishing boats. CCG and PLAN ships and a Chinese research vessel were nearby but did not interfere. The same kind of mission drew water cannon on 23–24 July.

22–26 Oct — Basilan Strait / off Mindanao: Westmincom tracked the Liaoning carrier group from northwest of Siocon (Zamboanga del Norte) to southwest of Maitum (Sarangani). It came within 15 nm (AFP) to 50 nm of the coast and did not answer radio challenges, and the AFP said there was 'no cause for alarm'.

20–23 Oct — Manila: Two Senate resolutions (Tulfo, Hontiveros) sought to declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan persona non grata. The Chinese Embassy dared lawmakers to 'stop bluffing', and on 23 Oct the DFA rebuked the embassy for its 'escalatory and undiplomatic' posts but stopped short of expelling him.

27–30 Oct — Cebu: The Philippines hosted ADMM-20 and ADMM-Plus. Defence Secretary Teodoro met US, Japanese, Australian and Vietnamese counterparts, and PCG spokesperson Tarriela rejected Chinese claims that the PCG presence was 'provocative'.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The quiet Scarborough fuel run eased tension slightly this week but does not change the underlying pattern. Since 8 Oct there has been water cannon against a medevac mission, an 11 Oct militia collision, CCG blocking at Pag-asa, and a carrier transit through Philippine archipelagic approaches. Over the next 90 days, expect continued CCG and militia pressure at Scarborough, Second Thomas Shoal, Pag-asa and Kota, PLA air intercepts, and more PLAN transits through the southern straits. The diplomatic row over Ambassador Jing could flare again if the executive moves on expulsion. A fatal incident or serious collision would raise the risk of Mutual Defense Treaty consultations. Mindanao and NPA violence on land remains low-level.

countries.name: South Korea
incidents: 29 Oct — East Sea: The military reported that North Korea fired an unidentified projectile off its eastern coast; the MND had released no further details.

27 Oct — Seoul: The JCS said North Korea appeared to be 'deploying and exposing its older artillery pieces along coastal areas' after Yonhap photographed three south-facing 122 mm howitzers across from Gimpo. The MND said it maintains 'a firm military readiness posture'. Newsis flagged viral 'Starbucks' photos of the guns as likely manipulated.

26 Oct — Seoul: The Unification Ministry said Pyongyang's UNSC letter aimed to justify its border fortification. The MND again proposed military talks to fix the MDL line and avoid accidental clashes, after Seoul's own letter to the UNSC called the mine placement a 'clear violation of the armistice agreement'.

1–24 Oct — DMZ: Kim Yo Jong said the South had fired 91 warning shots at MDL crossers in October, about 60 of them in three days; Seoul calls them legitimate defensive measures. The military has not ruled out resuming its own loudspeakers if the North switches on broadcasts.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Over the next 90 days, the DMZ is the main flashpoint. Exposed North Korean artillery within range of Gimpo, continuing MDL crossings met by warning fire, Pyongyang's 'self-defence' framing at the UN, and imminent loudspeaker broadcasts together create a real chance of an armed exchange. President Lee's government is caught between de-escalating and deterring, and is repeating its offer of MDL talks while domestic pressure for a firmer response grows. Watch for live fire across the MDL, a decision on Seoul's own loudspeakers, more mine or drone incidents, and the follow-on to the 29 Oct launch.

countries.name: Vietnam
incidents: 27–30 Oct — Cebu, Philippines: Defence Minister Phan Van Giang attended ADMM-20 and ADMM-Plus and met US Secretary of War Hegseth and the Australian, Japanese and Philippine defence ministers on 28 Oct. Hanoi welcomed US plans to show modern equipment at the Vietnam Defence Expo (10–13 Dec).

20–23 Oct — Hanoi: Vietnam held its first defence policy dialogue with Malaysia and pressed ahead with Vietnam–Laos–Cambodia defence cooperation, as Chinese military footprints on its western flank (Ream, Laos) remain a concern. No Vietnam–China maritime incident was reported between 22 and 29 Oct.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No incidents this week, but the underlying South China Sea dispute is unchanged. Over the next 90 days, Vietnam is likely to continue its two-track policy: political engagement with Beijing alongside quiet hedging through ASEAN, US, Japanese and Australian defence ties, and continued fortification of its Spratly features. Watch for Chinese pressure on Vietnamese fishermen in the Paracels, Chinese reactions to Vietnamese runway and port work in the Spratlys, and Vietnamese protests over the Antelope Reef and Yagong Island build-up. A direct naval confrontation remains unlikely.

countries.name: Japan
incidents: 20–23 Oct — Okinawa–Miyako gap / Sea of Japan: The Joint Staff recorded five foreign ISR flights during Keen Sword, three Chinese Y-9s through the Okinawa–Miyako gap (one reaching Amami Oshima) and two Russian Il-20s toward Shimane on 22–23 Oct. The JASDF scrambled fighters each time, and no airspace violation was reported.

19–29 Oct — Southwestern islands: Keen Sword 27 (about 45,000 JSDF and 11,000–12,000 US personnel plus seven partners) ran to 29 Oct. The new Type-25 anti-ship missile system was deployed mobile in the field, and the Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group joined in the Philippine Sea.
29 Oct — Sea of Japan: North Korea fired an unidentified projectile toward the East Sea on the final day of Keen Sword; no impact inside Japan's EEZ was reported.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained; watch for upgrade. Chinese and Russian ISR activity around Keen Sword stayed within routine-intercept bounds, and no Senkaku incident was reported this week. Over the next 90 days, expect continued Chinese drone, Y-9 and intelligence-ship transits of the Ryukyu gaps, possible Chinese–Russian joint bomber patrols, steady CCG presence around the Senkakus, and Chinese criticism of the Type-25 deployment. North Korean launches keep a risk of overflights or impacts in Japan's EEZ. A close-quarters air or maritime incident, a radar lock-on, or a missile landing in the EEZ would justify an upgrade to HIGH.

countries.name: Indonesia
incidents: 23 Oct — Yosoma village, Kenyam, Nduga, Highland Papua: Joint security forces, reportedly from the Rajawali VI task force, shot dead Masut Serera (25) and Helkia Kerebea (16) and wounded an 18-year-old. Six others were reportedly detained. A leaked police report found neither victim was an armed-group member, and Habema command expressed regret but said troops acted proportionately.

24 Oct — Nonggoloit, Kenyam, Nduga: The Habema joint operations command said troops exchanged fire with suspected TPNPB members and recovered air rifles, traditional weapons, communications gear and about IDR 88 million. No casualties were reported.

27 Oct — Dekai, Yahukimo, Highland Papua: A 35-year-old civilian was stabbed in the back near a kiosk and hospitalised. The Damai Cartenz task force is investigating a possible link to the Kodap XVI Yahukimo group of Kopi Tua Heluka, which is unconfirmed.

19 Oct — Papua (Damai Cartenz): Police said they had arrested 19 suspects since March for supplying firearms and ammunition to armed groups, and on the same day detained a man wanted over a 2021 camp arson in Puncak.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Lethal violence continues every week: civilians killed in a security operation in Nduga, firefights with the TPNPB, and attacks on non-Papuan civilians in Yahukimo. Over the next 90 days, expect TNI and police operations in Nduga, Intan Jaya, Puncak, Maybrat and Yahukimo with disputed casualty claims and more allegations of unlawful killings, displacement and alleged drone strikes. TPNPB attacks on civilians, drivers and people it labels informants will continue, especially in Yahukimo and along the Trans-Papua highway. Jakarta shows no sign of opening dialogue.

countries.name: Thailand
incidents: 28 Oct — Bangkok: Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Sihasak said Thailand is considering talks with Deep South groups beyond the BRN, either in parallel or within a widened process. This follows Malaysia's appointment of retired Lt Gen Ahmad Norihan Jalal as the new facilitator on 16–17 Oct; no date for the delayed round is confirmed.
